page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides dedicated CPU allocation with two threads per core alongside 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Total system memory is 8.0 GB, yielding a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. This machine type does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU capability, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2688.78 ranking in the upper quartile. Multi-threaded processing demonstrates consistent middle-tier output, logging a stress-ng multi-core score of 10787.62, a Geekbench multi-core score of 5770.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 11845.47. Cryptographic throughput is supported by instruction sets including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. Large block uncached memory throughput reaches 61.75 GB/sec for reads and 37.71 GB/sec for writes, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and overall PassMark memory scores sit in the lower quartile due to the compact memory envelope.

With a 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM gigabyte ratio, the instance provides cost-effective compute capacity for tasks that do not demand extensive working sets. Architectural tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe disks and the lack of AVX-512 extensions. The server is well configured for continuous integration runners, software compilation with Clang, containerized microservices, batch processing, and stateless web serving with static throughput measured at 7.56 GB/sec.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor featuring 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture. Designed with a lean 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance includes 8.0 GB of system memory, 32 MB of L3 cache, and dedicated core threads, with no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core CPU throughput on stress-ng alongside middle-tier multi-core execution in PassMark and Geekbench suites. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI flags, while memory operations show typical read and write bandwidth alongside lower PassMark memory scores. This instance provides a cost-effective compute envelope for workloads that require solid processor density without heavy memory overhead, such as compilation tasks, batch data processing, CI/CD build runners, and stateless web serving.
